concept.definition: WordPiece embeddings are subword-level token representations learned by first splitting text into a fixed-size vocabulary of common subword units using a data-driven segmentation algorithm, then mapping each subword to a dense vector.
concept.simpleExplanation: Instead of treating whole words as tokens, WordPiece breaks rare words into smaller, more common pieces (like 'play' into 'play' and '##ing'). This keeps the vocabulary manageable (30,000 tokens) and allows the model to handle any word by combining known subwords. The embedding for each subword is learned during pre-training.
concept.analogy: Think of building a toy set with Lego bricks: instead of having a separate mold for every possible toy car, you have a set of standard brick shapes. You can combine them to build almost any car, and the bricks themselves (the subwords) are reusable and shareable across different words.
concept.whyUsedHere: BERT uses WordPiece embeddings to balance vocabulary size and coverage: the 30,000 subword tokens are small enough for efficient training but large enough to represent any English text via composition. This avoids out-of-vocabulary problems and enables the model to learn meaningful subword-level patterns.
